questions.prompt: Summing n doubles in a std::vector and in a linked list are both O(n). Why is the list typically much slower for large n?
options: The list performs more floating-point additions than the vector does
Lists take more asymptotic steps because pointer chasing is O(n log n)
The vector is always held in registers while the list lives in memory
Nodes are scattered, so each hop is a cache miss and prefetching cannot help
questions.explanation: Both do n steps; the difference is the cost per step, dominated by memory latency for pointer chasing.

questions.prompt: Lines of 64 bytes. How many distinct cache lines does a sequential read of 2000 floats (4 bytes each, line-aligned start) touch? Give an integer.
A routine takes 3 ms at n=1000 and 12 ms at n=2000. Assuming t ~ n^p, what is p? Give a number with 1 decimal.
questions.explanation: Doubling n multiplied time by 4 = 2^p, so p = 2.

questions.prompt: 30% of a program's run time is spent in function f. You make f 5 times faster. What is the overall speedup? Give a number with 2 decimals.
What is the most important thing to do before optimizing a slow C++ program?
options: Turn on sanitizers, because they make the program run faster
Measure with an optimized build and a profiler to see where the time goes
Replace every vector with a linked list to avoid reallocation
Rewrite the hot loops with manual unrolling to help the optimizer
questions.explanation: Optimizing a function that takes a small fraction of the time cannot give a big gain (Amdahl's law).

questions.prompt: A benchmark loop computes a sum but never uses it, and the build is -O2. The reported time is 0 ns. Why?
options: The optimizer removed the dead computation
Timers cannot measure anything below one microsecond
The CPU cached the answer and never recomputed it
-O2 disables loops that have no side effects
questions.explanation: Make the result observable (volatile sink or print) so the work cannot be eliminated.

questions.prompt: Describe a trustworthy benchmark to compare a vector traversal with a linked-list traversal. Give at least five controls.
rubric: Optimized build, same data and result check, result consumed so the loop is not removed.
Allocation and setup outside the timed region; warm-up and repeated runs with median reported.
Several sizes spanning cache capacities; report ns per element and the machine/cache sizes.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
